summary.headline: V2 Retail Q2 FY27 revenue rose 28% to INR905.6 crores on volume growth, but SSSG was -14.9% reported and mgmt cut FY27 SSSG view to 5-7%.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue grew 28% YoY to INR905.6 crores, driven by 31% volume growth, with gross margin up 310 bps to 31.1% and pre-Ind AS EBITDA up 20% to INR53.4 crores. Reported SSSG was -14.9%, which management attributes mainly to the Durga Puja and wedding season shifting from Q2 to Q3; underlying SSSG was stated as +0.5%, and H1 calendar SSSG was -3.7%. Management opened 49 stores in Q2 (106 in H1, a record), and sales per square foot fell to INR700 per month from INR933. Management said it will open only 60-70 stores in H2, will open a total of 170-190 stores in FY27 (with some H2 sites slipping to April), and flagged that FY28 openings could fall to around 100 if Q3 trends stay weak.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR37 crores; mainly right-of-use assets for 106 new stores

segments.name: Category mix
segments.commentary: Men's wear about 40%, ladies 29%, kids 22%, lifestyle 9%; mix described as unchanged. Full-price sales 91% in Q2 and H1 vs 92% last year.

segments.name: Store network
segments.commentary: 427 stores across 27 states and 340+ cities as of 30 Sep 2026, about 4.6 million sq ft; 49 opened and 3 closed in Q2, 106 opened and 4 closed in H1. About 60% of new stores are in core states (UP, Bihar, MP, Odisha, Assam).

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guidance of 50%+ maintained; management said H2 revenue growth would need to be around 60%, with 7-9% SSSG from old stores and the rest from new stores.
FY27 SSSG guidance cut to 5-7% (from 8-10% for the rest of the year after H1 SSSG of -3.7%); Q3 SSSG target 5-7% on a period-to-period basis.

Full-year FY27 gross margin guided at 29-30%; post-Ind AS EBITDA margin 13.5-14.5% (management says it guides on pre-Ind AS); pre-Ind AS EBITDA margin guided at more than 7.5% for the full year, with H2 at least 8%.

Store openings: 60-70 in H2 FY27, taking FY27 total to 170-190; FY28 current guidance 120-150 stores, but could drop to about 100 if Q3 weak, with FY28 revenue growth then 35-40% vs about 50%. Decision point is end of Q3.
Net working capital expected to normalise to 75-80 days by March 2027; creditor days expected at 45-65 vs 65-70 average.
Q3 FY27 described as the company's best quarter ever in revenue and profitability.
capex_capacity: Opened 106 stores in H1 FY27, which management called its highest-ever H1 addition; plans 60-70 more in H2 and says back end (design, sourcing, warehousing, talent) can support 150+ stores per year.
About 18 of the H2 pipeline already opened; remainder to shift to April 2027 due to site project delays.
Closing retail space up about 1 million sq ft since March 2026; inventory rose to INR1,447.8 crores from INR1,141 crores at March 2026.
V2Kart e-commerce piloted in 2 states; operational issues with fulfilling single-piece orders from about 35,000 pieces of stock per store; expansion to more states pending.
demand_pricing: Reported SSSG -14.9% in Q2; underlying +0.5% after festive shift; H1 calendar SSSG -3.7%. Sales per sq ft per month INR700 in Q2 (vs INR933) and INR785 in H1 (vs INR948).
Mature stores (over 2 years) at INR1,000+ PSF; new stores at about INR720-730 on a last-12-month basis, 35-40% below mature stores. Management said Q2 PSF is typically 40-45% below year average.
October: calendar basis double-digit SSSG growth; period-to-period (Dussehra-to-Dussehra) flat. Winter fill rate about 20% better than last year.

Average bill value INR917 in H1 (vs INR900); ABV down about 1% and footfall down about 3% in Q2 per management. ASP about INR307 vs INR309; ASP down 3% in H1 as product mix shifted to value and economy.
Price increases: input costs up 3-7%; MRP raised 5-10% to protect gross margin. Shift to blended fabrics. Management said it will take further hikes only if raw material prices rise again.

Competitors named: unorganised mom-and-pop stores and organised players such as V-Mart, Style Baazar, Citykart, Baazar Kolkata and M Baazar. Management said its PSF is at least 30% above its closest competitor in most locations.

Repeat customers in mature stores rose from 55% to about 70%; repeat frequency fell from 5-5.5 months to 4.4-4.5 months; marketing cost under 0.5% of revenue; loyal customer spend INR2,200-2,500 a year.

qa_highlights.question: Break-up of Q2 negative LFL by festival-dependent states vs other states, and October/November trends?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not have the state split; about 260 stores are Puja-impacted. October calendar growth was more than double-digit but flat period-to-period; management will update around mid-December.

qa_highlights.question: Is the store addition slowing to H2 and does the 50% growth guidance still hold?
qa_highlights.answer: About 18 of the H2 pipeline is already open, with 60-70 more planned and the rest shifting to April on project delays. Management said it has not changed the 50%+ revenue growth guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Is there an underlying demand problem beyond the festive shift?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no single factor stands out: ABV, ASP, state-wise and cohort-wise SSSG all showed the same slowdown, and competitor benchmarking showed similar results. Demand softened in the last three months.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company cut store additions if SSSG stays weak?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, if the trend continues through Q3, FY28 openings would be about 100 instead of 150-200, with revenue growth falling to 35-40%. The decision will be taken at end-Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Why did new-store PSF fall to about INR700 from the INR938 level last quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: PSF is a last-12-month average; new stores are about INR720-730 on that basis, and Q2 is seasonally 40-45% lower. Management said the 12-month average for new stores is still above INR730-740.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margin up 300 bps despite lower full-price share; what drove it, and what is the full-year view?
qa_highlights.answer: Average discount depth fell to about 30% from 50%, a bill-buster promotion moved from Q2 last year to Q3 this year, and Q1 margin was 1% lower due to earlier discounting for Adhik Maas. Full-year gross margin guided at 29-30%.

qa_highlights.question: Debt has risen to about INR500 crores; what level is comfortable?
qa_highlights.answer: Borrowings were INR528 crores (INR483 crores current). Management said debt-to-equity below 0.5 is healthy if EBITDA covers interest, and expects borrowings to ease as store additions slow.

qa_highlights.question: Will Q3 be the best quarter ever and what is the margin path?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed Q3 will be the best quarter ever in revenue and profitability. Full-year pre-Ind AS EBITDA margin should be above 7.5%, with H2 at least 8% versus about 7% in H1.

risks_watch: Reported SSSG of -14.9% in Q2 and H1 calendar SSSG of -3.7%; demand slowed in the last three months per management, with no single cause identified.
Working capital: inventory of INR1,447.8 crores, net working capital 88 days vs 81 days, and borrowings up to INR528 crores; normalisation targeted for March 2027 (75-80 days).
Store productivity: new stores at about 35-40% lower PSF than mature stores; management has stretched the maturity period for FY25 cohorts to 2.5-3.5 years.
Q3 festive and winter season is the test: October flat period-to-period; management will reassess store openings at end-Q3.
Depreciation rising sharply (INR68 crores vs INR37 crores) and expected to keep rising in Q3 and Q4 as store base grows.
Creditor days to fall to 45-65 days from 65-70 as cash is used for early vendor payments.
Input cost inflation of 3-7%; further price increases possible if raw material costs rise; V2Kart e-commerce still at pilot stage in 2 states.
Governance/disclosure: an analyst raised repeatedly the non-disclosure of the core senior team (6-7 people) and mature-store SSSG for H1; management committed to share in a future presentation.
key_quotes: So we checke d the data and nothing stands out in particular.
But in the last 3 months, definitely we saw some sort of a demand slowdown.
Yes, correct. So if this trend continues to the third quarter, then next year we'll only open 100 stores, which initially the target was 150 to 200.
Yes, I think we are not changing our guidance in terms of revenue growth.
Yes, Q3 will be V2 Retail's best quarter ever. In terms of revenue, in terms of profitability, correct.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term store roll-out, back-end readiness and Q3 recovery, but cautious and somewhat defensive on near-term demand: he attributed Q2 SSSG mainly to the festive shift, said the last three months showed a demand slowdown with no single cause identified, and repeatedly declined to give mature-store H1 SSSG or the core team names on the call.
